sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the layout, text input, pop-up, alert and loading pieces, icons, shared styles and parts, and the family store that holds profiles and sharing.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup for the screen and its store.

sections.name: FamilyManagementScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Header, loading and form actions
sections.what: Shows the title, a subtitle, and the add button. On open it loads profiles. Creating a member uses the typed name and relationship, then closes the form. Sharing uses the typed email with view access and shows a success or error alert.
sections.why: Likely reason: each form has a matching action, and errors are shown as alerts so the user knows what happened.
sections.watch_out: A failed share shows one general message, so the user cannot tell whether the email or the server was at fault.

sections.name: FamilyManagementScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Managed and shared profile lists
sections.what: Lists the profiles the user manages, each with a letter avatar, name, relationship and a share button. Below, if any exist, it lists profiles other people have shared with the user, with their access level.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates profiles the user controls from profiles others have given them.
sections.watch_out: The avatar reads the first character of the name, which fails if the name is missing.

sections.name: FamilyManagementScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Add member and share pop-up forms
sections.what: Two pop-up forms. The add form takes a name and one of three relationships (parent, child or spouse), with Create Profile and Cancel buttons. The share form takes an email address, with Send Invite and Cancel buttons, and shows the name of the profile being shared.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the forms hidden until they are needed.
sections.watch_out: Text typed into a form stays after Cancel, so the next time the form opens it still shows the old entry.

sections.name: FamilyManagementScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Style definitions for the family screen
sections.what: Holds the visual rules for the family screen: header, member rows, avatar circles, and the add-member popup with its input box and relationship buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the look of the screen separate from the layout code, so the screen is easier to adjust.

summary: Lets a user see the health profiles they manage for family members, add a new family member, and share a profile with someone by email.
purpose: Supports caregiving: one person can look after another person's health records, and can let someone else view them.
why: Likely reason: people often manage the records of parents or children, and sharing by email is a simple way to give view access.
how: When the screen opens it loads profiles from the family store. It lists the profiles the user manages, then profiles shared with the user. The plus button opens a form for a name and relationship (parent, child or spouse). The share icon on a managed profile opens a form for an email address, and sending it calls shareAccess with view-only access.
inputs: A name and relationship typed by the user, an email address typed by the user, and profile data from the family store.
outputs: New family profiles created through addMember, share requests sent through shareAccess, and success or error alerts.
risks: Sharing gives view access to whoever owns that email. The email is not checked for a valid format before sending. Cancelling a form keeps the typed text for next time. The avatar uses the first letter of the name, which fails if the name is empty. Only view access can be given.
debug: If profiles do not appear, check fetchProfiles and the family store. If sharing says user not found, check the email spelling and whether that person has an account. If adding fails, check addMember and the network call behind it. If sharing fails unexpectedly, check shareAccess and the server's reply.
